bustools 0.45.1 – one program for all its commands (sort, correct, count, text, inspect, capture, whitelist or
allowlist, umicorrect, compress, decompress and the others)
Licence: BSD 2-Clause (LICENSE in this folder; copyright BUStools). bustools contains CRoaring 0.2.65 (Apache 2.0:
LICENSE.CRoaring), Eigen 3.3.7 (MPL 2.0, with parts under BSD: LICENSE.eigen, LICENSE.eigen.BSD, LICENSE.eigen.README;
built with EIGEN_MPL2_ONLY, so no part under the LGPL is in it), kseq (MIT: LICENSE.kseq), CppNumericalSolvers (MIT:
LICENSE.CppNumericalSolvers) and LBFGSpp (MIT: LICENSE.LBFGSpp), and is linked with zlib 1.3.1 (LICENSE.zlib). The
loader is Emscripten's runtime (MIT and NCSA: LICENSE.emscripten). THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt is genomics-wasm's summary;
the "sources/" it mentions is that project's folder.
Upstream source: https://github.com/BUStools/bustools (commit d4d7a283dbe9d34d2106e9ba31e2566413be6a70, which is version
0.45.1). The source code, as GitHub's archive of that commit (SHA-256
b014317ea4501c3314ac358eb074dbbe3a10ed6daec53587f17a897e670e40df; it holds Eigen's source, which the Mozilla Public
License asks to be offered with the program): ../../../licenses/sources/bustools-0.45.1.tar.gz. zlib 1.3.1:
../../../licenses/sources/zlib-1.3.1.tar.gz (the same files as the archive of its tag v1.3.1 that was compiled, which
adds only .github/ and .gitignore). The changes made to bustools:
../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/tools/bustools/browser.patch.

Compiled to WebAssembly by the genomics-wasm project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, commit
46c9418): Emscripten 3.1.64, one thread, no SIMD. bustools.mjs and bustools.wasm are used here as that project built
them. The page runs each command in a worker of its own (assets/js/threads-worker.mjs); assets/js/tools-wasm.js gives it
its files. Everything needed to build it again is described in ../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/.

Changes to the source (browser.patch): sort uses 64 MB of memory unless told otherwise, and at most 1 GB (upstream's
default, 4 GB, is more than a 32-bit program can address) – the terminal turns a larger -m into -m 64M, with a note;
sort takes one thread – the terminal turns -t N into -t 1, with a note; predict runs its per-gene work in order instead
of in threads; two bit shifts are made safe for a 32-bit program (one of them in the BUSZ format, which stays that of
the native program); and the mean number of reads per UMI of a cell with no reads, 0/0, is written as Linux's bustools
writes it (-nan), whatever sign the WebAssembly engine gives that NaN. Sorting, correction, counting, UMI correction and
compression are unchanged.

Checked against bustools 0.45.1 built natively from the same source (genomics-wasm's comparison: 56 of 56 cases – every
command, files written by one build and read by the other, errors), and in the workbench, against the native program,
with the example data (single-cell RNA-seq of mouse cells, SRA run SRR8599150): the same BUS files, text, corrected and
sorted records, matrices, barcode and gene lists, compressed files and messages (but for the times that sort prints),
byte for byte – and for one file: the .ec.txt that count writes without --genecounts lists the same equivalence classes,
and those that the matrix uses have the same numbers, but the others can be numbered in another order (bustools keeps
them in an unordered_map, whose order depends on the C++ library: libc++ here, libstdc++ on Linux).
